Definition: Whether primary laws, acts, or legal instruments exist that establish authority for cross-government data sharing and govern the data exchange system
Comments: No comprehensive law governing cross-government data sharing. Electronic Transactions Act 2007 and Cybercrime Acts exist. No dedicated data protection law. Three new digital authorities created by PM decree in Nov 2025 but no legislative basis for data exchange.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Sudan still has no primary legislation establishing cross-government data-sharing authority. A November 2025 PM decree created a Digital Transformation Authority, a Data and AI Authority, and a Cybersecurity Authority under the Ministry of Digital Transformation and Communications, but these are administrative bodies, not enabling legislation for data exchange; a 2018 draft Data Protection Bill remains unenacted. Only sectoral instruments (Electronic Transactions Act 2007, Cybercrime Act 2007) exist. Score of 1 (No) confirmed and vintage updated to reflect the November 2025 decree.
revised_comments: Sudan has no primary law establishing authority for cross-government data sharing. A Prime Ministerial decree of November 2025 created three digital authorities (Digital Transformation, Data and AI, and Cybersecurity) under the Ministry of Digital Transformation and Communications to advance e-government, but this is an administrative restructuring rather than legislation governing a data exchange system. Sectoral laws (Electronic Transactions Act 2007, Cybercrime Act 2007) address electronic transactions and cybercrime but not cross-government data sharing, and a 2018 draft Data Protection Bill has never been enacted amid continuing conflict and political instability.

Definition: Provisions ensuring national control over government data and protecting against unauthorized foreign access
Comments: No data protection legislation. UNDP Compass Data and Privacy at 2.92 (functional data protection authority/regulation in recognition stage), but in practice no laws restricting cross-border data transfer. Electronic Transactions Act 2007 and Cybercrime Acts exist but do not address data sovereignty comprehensively.
revision_notes: Confirmed. Sudan has no comprehensive data-protection or data-localisation legislation and no independent data protection authority, so there are no enforceable controls restricting cross-border transfer of government data or protecting against unauthorised foreign access. Article 54 of the 2019 Constitutional Charter provides only a general privacy guarantee, and a 2018 draft Data Protection Bill has never been passed. Score of 1 (No controls) confirmed; no fresher legislative development identified as of 2025/2026.
revised_comments: Sudan has no enforceable data sovereignty or localisation provisions. There is no comprehensive data protection law and no independent data protection authority to regulate cross-border transfers of government or personal data; protection rests only on a general constitutional privacy guarantee (Article 54, 2019 Constitutional Charter) and sectoral electronic transactions and cybercrime laws that do not address data sovereignty. A 2018 draft Data Protection Bill has never been enacted, leaving national control over government data largely unregulated in practice.

Definition: Whether data exchange infrastructure and services reach rural and remote areas or concentrate in urban centers
Comments: UNDP Compass notes physical infrastructure at Stage 2 (inaccessible, basic quality, selective coverage). World Bank 2022 diagnostic notes skewed geographic concentration of digital infrastructure. Conflict has worsened this divide.
revision_notes: Confirmed and worsened. Telecom infrastructure and coverage remain heavily concentrated in Khartoum and other major cities; a 2024 SMEX analysis of Zain and MTN network maps shows rural areas (63.8% of the population) are largely unserved. The 2023-25 civil war has further degraded rural connectivity through destroyed infrastructure fuel and power shortages and deliberate service cuts documented in Freedom House's 2024 and 2025 Freedom on the Net reports with 62.7% of the population rural per DataReportal's late-2025 estimate. Score of 1 (Primarily urban) confirmed with newer conflict-era evidence.
revised_comments: Data exchange and broader digital infrastructure in Sudan remain concentrated in Khartoum and a handful of major urban centres, with rural areas (roughly 63% of the population) receiving markedly weaker mobile network coverage and unreliable maintenance. The 2023-2025 civil war has intensified this divide: fighting has destroyed telecommunications infrastructure, caused prolonged blackouts in cities such as Wad Madani and Khartoum, and left large rural and conflict-affected areas such as Darfur and Kordofan with minimal or no connectivity. Unreliable electricity supply, itself concentrated away from rural areas, compounds the gap, leaving rural connectivity dependent on costly satellite alternatives such as Starlink where available.
